title: Generated serving Dockerfiles must bound apt timeouts and retries before installing packages
answers: serving image build hangs forever on apt-get update
docker build for model serving stuck on package mirror
apt-get install never finishes when Ubuntu mirror stalls
generated Dockerfile apt retries and timeouts
body:
Symptom: A serving-image build (docker build of a generated MLflow model Dockerfile) hangs indefinitely while apt fetches packages from a stalled Ubuntu mirror.
Root cause: mlflow/models/docker_utils.py:generate_dockerfile emitted apt-get update/install with no socket timeout or retry config, so apt never reached its retry logic.
Fix pattern: Prepend the SETUP_APT_TIMEOUTS block (writes Acquire::http/https::Timeout "30" and Acquire::Retries "3" to /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99-mlflow-timeouts) before any apt-get RUN in the MLflow-controlled python-slim and UBUNTU_BASE_IMAGE branches.
Constraints: Applies only to MLflow-controlled base images; caller-supplied custom base images must stay unchanged. Keep the config file ahead of the apt-get update RUN, or the setting is not in effect for that install.
applies: Dockerfile generation in mlflow/models/docker_utils.py for serving images; not for user-provided base images.
says: Building the model serving container image hangs indefinitely during package installation.
Docker builds for model deployment get stuck when package mirrors fail to respond.
Add retry limits and download timeouts to package managers in generated serving images.
Container builds for served models never finish if an operating system mirror stalls.
search: Generated model serving Dockerfiles must configure apt network timeouts and retry limits before running package installation commands. In mlflow/models/docker_utils.py:generate_dockerfile, SETUP_APT_TIMEOUTS configures Acquire::http/https::Timeout "30" and Acquire::Retries "3" in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99-mlflow-timeouts prior to any apt-get RUN instruction. This applies to MLflow-controlled python-slim and UBUNTU_BASE_IMAGE branches but leaves user-provided custom base images unchanged. The configuration must precede apt-get update to ensure timeout limits apply to that installation.
